subject: How to generate a random value in the equations without sampling error?

messages.subject: How to generate a random value in the equations without sampling error?
parts:
Greetings,

I encounter a problem when I try to generate a random value as a part of the equations.

The central idea of the model is correcting the endogenous problem in X with an additional variable, w.
The model are expressed in the following: 
X = mu*pi + v; where pi represents the category. X can locate in one of the category and mu is the category mean.
Y = alpha + beta*X +w; This is a normal linear regression. 
where v, w are the error term distributed as N(0,tau) and N(0,sigma) respectively.
Moreover: v/sqrt(tau) = rou*w/sqrt(sigma) + sqrt(1-rou^2)*z where z is standard normal distribution, rou is the correlation between v and w. (v and w are bivariate normal distributed) 

How to express the above relationship is the central of my problem. I am not sure whether I am able to generate random number z as a part of the equation and how to express w properly. The error message is "Exception thrown at line XX: stan::math::normal_log: Random variable is nan, but must not be nan!"

I know that if I specify two finite mixture normal model (with X and Y), the model will run successfully and correctly. However, I want to extend the model to the logit model case. Then, Y will become the latent Utility. I hope I can use U = X*beta + w; y[i]~categorical_logit(U) at the end. (This expression/The simple logit regression was successfully implemented before.) That's why I am trying to find an alternative expression to solve the endogenous problem on a linear regression with simulated data.

I appreciate any suggestions/comments. Thank you very much for reading these illustrations!

for(k in 1:3) {

        }
    }  // simple store the value

    for (obss in 1:N){

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: How to generate a random value in the equations without sampling error?
parts:
On Sunday, September 25, 2016 at 4:17:13 PM UTC-4, Sherry He wrote:
I encounter a problem when I try to generate a random value as a part of the equations.

The premise that you can generate an unknown in the model block of a Stan program is not correct. To do something like this, you need to declare (a vector) z in the parameters block of the Stan program

parameters {
  ...
  vector[N] z;
  ...
}

then doing

z ~ normal(0, 1);

in the model block will work, although you would be less likely to confuse yourself about this point if you use the new notation

target += normal_lpdf(z | 0, 1);

which makes it more explicit that all the model block of a Stan program is doing is building up a log-posterior kernel (of which this standard normal prior on the elements of z is one piece). Given this log-posterior kernel, HMC is able to evolve through the parameter space to produce draws from the joint posterior distribution. There is no marginal generation of unknowns, except in the generated quantities block.

Ben
